You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

Solicitation ID: 3202600155

Extract the full compliance matrix from the attached RFP. Work through the document section by section; do not stop until you have covered the final page, including attachments and exhibits that contain vendor obligations.

ARTICLE I PURPOSE 
The Texas Workforce Commission (TWC) is seeking Applications from qualified

areas of the state. Applicants must meet all requirements and specifications 
outlined herein to be eligible to provide services. 
The TWC Procurement Services (PS) section will administer the procurement 
process for this Open Enrollment, which includes Open Enrollment publication, 
handling of communications from Applicants, as well as managing the receipt 
of Applications for review. 
Information regarding TWC and its programs is available online and can be 
currently accessed at www.twc.texas.gov.

ARTICLE II SCOPE OF WORK 
2.1 OVERVIEW OF ORIENTATION AND MOBILITY SERVICES 
TWC’s mission is to promote and support a workforce system that creates 
value and offers employers, families, individuals and communities the 
opportunity to achieve and sustain economic prosperity. 
Orientation and Mobility (O&M) services prepare blind and visually impaired 
customers to travel independently with competence and confidence. 
This Open Enrollment is for O&M Services. O&M services prepare blind and 
visually impaired customers to travel independently with competence and 
confidence. 
O&M specialists offer complex, interrelated services designed to develop 
independent travel skills in individuals who are blind or visually impaired. O&M 
services begin with an assessment and can include training held in 
environments frequently visited by customers. 
Orientation is the process of using the available senses to establish one's 
position and relationship within the environment. 
Mobility is the ability to travel in the environment with the help of an 
established tool (including white canes, dog guides, and electronic travel aids). 
O&M assessments and training can be provided in locations within the 
customer's home or community. O&M assessments and training are provided 
in person and cannot be provided remotely. 
Examples of training locations include: 
1. the customer's home (indoor and outdoor); 
2. public areas, such as a bank, church, or doctor's office; 
3. commercial areas, such as a grocery store or mall;

[page 11]
Open Enrollment for No. 3202600155 Orientation and Mobility v. 1.1 
Page 11 of 50 
4. transit systems, such as public transportation, paratransit, and taxis; 
5. rural areas; 
6. residential areas (with light traffic and stop signs); 
7. small business areas (with heavier traffic and simple traffic lights); 
8. downtown areas (with heavy traffic and complex traffic lights); and 
9. commercial modes of travel, such as trains and planes. 
All fees for services described in this chapter can be found in VR-SFP 5.5 
Orientation and Mobility Service Fees. 
2.2 PROVIDER REQUIREMENTS, RESPONSIBILITIES, AND TWC 
POLICIES

requirements, and TWC policies applicable to them. 
2.3 VR STANDARDS FOR PROVIDERS (VR-SFP) MANUAL 
The VR Standards for Providers (VR-SFP) Manual focuses on the business 
practices, processes, and policies that must be followed for TWC and the 
Provider to comply with federal and state laws and TWC rules and 
requirements. Providers must adhere to the current VR-SFP Manual when 
providing services to VR Customers. 
An Applicant applying for a contract must comply with the following VR-SFP 
Manual chapters in addition to the Solicitation. 
• Chapter 1: Introduction to Vocational Rehabilitation 
• Chapter 2: Obtaining a Contract for Goods and Services 
• Chapter 3: Basic Standards 
Notice of upcoming changes to the VR-SFP Manual are published on the

[page 12]

Page 12 of 50 
Vocational Rehabilitation Providers’ Resources page at least thirty (30) 
calendar days in advance of the effective date of the changes. Each Provider is 
contractually responsible for maintaining compliance with the most current VR-
SFP Manual. 
A revision list that summarizes any formal changes to the VR-SFP Manual can 
be found on the Vocational Rehabilitation Standards for Providers Revision Log. 
TWC GovDelivery notifies Providers every time revisions are posted to the VR-
SFP Manual and other important information. All Providers should subscribe to 
TWC GovDelivery list to gain these notifications. Visit the TWC GovDelivery 
website, enter an email address, and select the topic “Vocational Rehabilitation 
Contractors and Providers News” to subscribe. 
For questions about the content in the VR-SFP email, contact 
vr.standards@twc.texas.gov. 
2.4 REQUIREMENTS 
2.4.1 Qualifications and Training  
Before services are provided, the service provider director must: 
• approve VR3455, Provider Staff Information Form, which is completed by 
each of the provider's staff members, such as specialists and interns (the 
form must include the staff members' qualifications as stated in Section 
2.4.2 Orientation and Mobility Specialist and provide evidence that 
the staff member meets the qualifications); and 
• submit the approved form to the provider's assigned contract manager 
and assigned regional program specialist. 
2.4.2 Orientation and Mobility Specialist  
The O&M specialist must meet one of the following criteria:

[page 13]
Open Enrollment for No. 3202600155 Orientation and Mobility v. 1.1 
Page 13 of 50 
• Be certified by the Academy for Certification of Vision Rehabilitation and 
Education Professionals (ACVREP) or the National Blindness Professional 
Certification Board (NBPCB); 
• Have a degree in O&M from an accredited college or university with an 
established O&M training curriculum and become certified by ACVREP or 
NBPCB within one (1) year of being hired by a service provider; 
• Have at least two (2) years of full-time experience teaching O&M skills 
for an entity that VR recognizes, such as a rehabilitation center, a 
Veterans Administration hospital, or an educational system, and: 
o provide three (3) professional references indicating the candidate's 
ability to teach O&M skills to blind or visually impaired individuals; 
and 
o be certified by ACVREP or NBPCB within one year of being hired by 
the service provider. 
2.4.2.1 REQUIRED TEXAS CONFIDENCE BUILDERS TRAINING FOR O&M 
SPECIALISTS 
In addition to meeting the requirements for education, training, and 
experience described in Section 2.4.2 Orientation and Mobility Specialist, 
all prospective O&M providers must successfully complete the Orientation and 
Mobility Texas Confidence Builders training before becoming providers. 
Texas Confidence Builders training is a two- to three-day training program 
offered in Austin. While the training is provided free of cost, providers must 
pay all costs associated with attending the training program. Contact the state 
office O&M program specialist to schedule the training. 
2.4.3 Annual Staff Training  
To ensure that O&M specialists remain competent in their skills, VR

[page 14]
Open Enrollment for No. 3202600155 Orientation and Mobility v. 1.1 
Page 14 of 50 
recommends that each O&M trainer complete a minimum of twenty (20) hours 
of blindfold travel per fiscal year, so that the O&M trainer: 
• practices his or her own independent travel skills; 
• provides effective role modeling; and 
• promotes independent travel as a confidence-building tool for customers. 
Examples of recommended activities for blindfold travel include: 
• traveling around a city block; 
• traveling on an L-shaped sidewalk route; 
• traveling to the grocery store; and 
• exploring a new neighborhood. 
VR also recommends O&M specialists: 
• create a report like the Sample Orientation and Mobility Provider's 
Independent Travel Activity Report; and 
• send a copy of their travel activity report to the assigned regional 
program specialist for VR. 
2.4.4 Orientation and Mobility Interns 
O&M service providers are ultimately responsible for the monitoring, 
supervision, and follow-up of the O&M intern during the internship. 
O&M service providers using interns to work with VR customers must: 
• have an O&M specialist with ACVREP or NBPCB certification observe each 
intern for a minimum of twelve (12) lessons during the internship and 
document the observations on VR2922, Orientation and Mobility Weekly 
Internship Observation; 
• submit VR2922 to the regional program support specialist each month

[page 15]

during the internship; and 
• submit VR2923, Orientation and Mobility Internship Performance 
Evaluation to the designated regional program specialist within thirty-five 
(35) days of completion of the internship. 
The O&M intern must: 
• attend Texas Confidence Builders training in Austin or attend another 
approved training with the VR in-house O&M designee before working 
with blind and visually impaired customers; 
• be supervised by an approved VR-certified O&M provider for the duration 
of the internship; 
• be observed by a VR-certified O&M provider for a minimum of twelve 
(12) lessons during the internship; and 
• sign and then forward reports to the supervising O&M provider that 
maintains either the ACVREP or NBPCB for his or her approval. 
Note: VR does not pay for any expenses incurred by the intern during the 
internship. 
2.4.5 Orientation and Mobility Service Assessment  
The following sections describe the O&M Service assessment and expectations. 
2.4.5.1 ORIENTATION AND MOBILITY ASSESSMENT SERVICE DESCRIPTION  
The assessment includes an evaluation of the customer's O&M skills in multiple 
situations in person and cannot be conducted remotely. 
Assessments may be conducted using the customer's functional vision. 
Functional vision refers to the way in which an individual uses whatever vision 
he or she has in a given travel situation. Assessments provide an opportunity 
for customers to recognize that their vision might not meet all their travel

[page 16]
Open Enrollment for No. 3202600155 Orientation and Mobility v. 1.1 
Page 16 of 50 
needs. 
Locations for assessments include a combination of: 
1. the customer's home and immediate surrounding area; 
2. public areas, such as a church, park, or college campus; 
3. commercial areas, such as a bank, store, or mall; 
4. transit systems, such as paratransit or taxis (if available); 
5. local buses and similar public transportation (if available); 
6. rural areas (if applicable); 
7. residential areas (those with light vehicle and foot traffic and some stop 
signs); 
8. small business areas (those with heavier traffic and simple traffic 
lights); 
9. downtown areas (those with heavy vehicle and foot traffic and complex 
traffic lights); 
10. commercial transportation systems, such as buses, trains, and 
airplanes (if applicable); and 
11. travel using low-vision devices (if applicable). 
For Independent Living Services for Older Individuals Who Are Blind (OIB) 
customers, the OIB worker authorizes a maximum of three (3) hours for the 
initial assessment to be completed. 
The O&M specialist must include in the initial assessment observations of and 
recommendations on white cane skills. The recommended number of hours 
allowed for training must include the customer's travel needs, regardless of the 
mobility tool (dog or white cane). Training with a guide dog must not exceed 
more than four hours and must be preapproved in writing by the VR counselor

[page 17]
Open Enrollment for No. 3202600155 Orientation and Mobility v. 1.1 
Page 17 of 50 
or OIB worker. 
Recommendations for training must be: 
• documented under the summary section of VR2894, Orientation and 
Mobility Assessment; and 
• submitted to the VR counselor or OIB worker. 
Following the assessment, it is recommended that the O&M specialist reviews 
the results with the customer and answers any questions that the customer 
might have about the recommended training. 
2.4.5.2 PROCESS AND PROCEDURE 
The VR counselor or OIB worker completes the VR2897, Orientation and 
Mobility Referral, leaving no blanks and putting NA (not applicable) as needed. 
After completion of the form, the VR counselor or OIB worker sends it to the 
provider that has been chosen by the customer. Included with the referral is 
information that helps the O&M specialist assess and recommend training for 
the customer. 
The VR counselor or OIB worker is responsible for authorizing an O&M 
assessment and approving services, including approving the documentation for 
payment when invoiced. 
Based on the results of the O&M assessment, the VR counselor or OIB worker 
determines the training goal and hours to be funded by VR or OIB. No 
assessments or training sessions are completed before a service authorization 
is issued. 
After submitting VR2894, Orientation and Mobility Assessment, the O&M 
specialist must contact the customer's VR counselor or OIB worker to discuss 
the initial assessment. This discussion must be documented and filed in the 
O&M provider's customer file.

[page 18]
Open Enrollment for No. 3202600155 Orientation and Mobility v. 1.1

The discussion includes: 
• the O&M specialist's recommendations for training (if any), including the: 
o O&M skills needed; 
o proposed completion date; and 
o number of training hours authorized by the customer's VR 
counselor or OIB worker; 
• anticipated delays in services, if any; 
• special considerations or extended direct training dates, if any; 
• the customer's readiness to begin nonvisual O&M skills training; and 
• the customer's understanding of O&M skills training and its potential 
benefits. 
2.4.5.3 OUTCOMES REQUIRED FOR PAYMENT  
The O&M provider documents in descriptive terms the information required on 
the VR2894, Orientation and Mobility Assessment, including: 
• the O&M specialist's observations and comments; 
• recommendations for O&M skills training; 
• the number of training hours recommended for each area of training and 
the total number of training hours recommended; 
• the anticipated beginning and ending dates for the recommended 
training; 
• the customer's response to the training recommendations; 
• the height of the white cane that is most appropriate for the customer 
(using the measurement between the customer's chin and nose when

[page 19]
Open Enrollment for No. 3202600155 Orientation and Mobility v. 1.1 
Page 19 of 50 
the customer is standing up); and 
• a description of all travel aids that the customer uses or would benefit 
from using. 
2.4.6 Orientation and Mobility Training 
The following sections describe how O&M is provided to the client after an 
evaluation. 
2.4.6.1 ORIENTATION AND MOBILITY TRAINING SERVICE DESCRIPTION  
O&M training prepares an individual who is blind or visually impaired to travel 
independently with competence and confidence. 
Based on the results of the evaluation, the VR counselor or OIB worker 
determines the training goal and hours to be funded by VR or OIB. No training 
is provided before a service authorization is issued. Training is provided in 
person and cannot be conducted remotely. 
All O&M training services for VR customers are conducted using: 
• nonvisual (blindfold) techniques; and 
• a rigid (non-folding) white cane with a metal tip. 
All O&M training services for OIB customers are conducted using: 
• either nonvisual (blindfold) or visual training, whichever better addresses 
the customer's needs and circumstances; and 
• a rigid (non-folding) white cane with a metal tip, unless an alternate 
cane is needed. 
The O&M specialist must discuss the benefits of nonvisual and visual training 
with each customer. Role modeling and peer support for nonvisual training are 
encouraged.

[page 20]
Open Enrollment for No. 3202600155 Orientation and Mobility v. 1.1 
Page 20 of 50 
The O&M specialist may not conduct more than six (6) hours or fewer than two 
(2) hours of O&M instruction per day. The O&M specialist cannot conduct more 
than six (6) hours of training in a day, even if multiple customers are served 
during that day. Billing for O&M services must not exceed six (6) hours per 
day. Lessons are at least two (2) hours long unless approved by an obtained 
VR3472, Contracted Service Modification Request for Blind and Visually 
Impaired Services. 
For Independent Living Services for Older Individuals Who Are Blind (ILS-OIB) 
customers, the length of the training lesson will be determined by the 
customer’s health, stamina, and ability to participate. 
2.4.6.2 PROCESS AND PROCEDURE 
The following details the specific processes and procedures involved in O&M 
Training services. 
2.4.6.2.1 GENERAL 
The VR counselor or OIB worker is responsible for authorizing O&M training for 
the customer and approving services, including approving the documentation 
for payment when invoiced. 
The provider must not bill for any services other than Orientation and Mobility 
training, or Orientation and Mobility group training. 
Based on the results of the assessment, the VR counselor or OIB worker 
determines the training goals and hours to be funded by VR or OIB. No 
training is provided before a service authorization is issued. 
O&M training must not exceed the total number of training hours and type of 
training authorized by the customer's VR counselor or OIB worker on the 
service authorization. 
Consistent and frequent scheduling is recommended to maximize learning.

[page 21]
Open Enrollment for No. 3202600155 Orientation and Mobility v. 1.1 
Page 21 of 50 
One two-hour lesson a week is the minimum training allowable. Daily O&M 
training is considered best practice. 
Note: For OIB customers, if less than two (2) hours of training were provided 
in one (1) session, the trainer must document on the VR2896 in the Brief 
Description of how the training lesson affected the customer’s health, stamina, 
and ability to participate. 
Time spent transporting customers does not count toward training time. O&M 
specialists are not reimbursed for time spent in the car, even when a customer 
is present. 
The O&M specialist must notify the customer's VR counselor or OIB worker 
within 24 hours about all: 
• missed, cancelled, or rescheduled appointments; 
• issues, concerns, or circumstances that might impact or delay planned 
services; and 
• incidents or injuries that occur during training that might negatively 
impact the customer's health and safety.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.

ARTICLE II SCOPE OF WORK 
2.1 OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND 
TWC’s mission is to promote and support a workforce system that creates 
value and offers employers, families, individuals and communities the 
opportunity to achieve and sustain economic prosperity. 
This Open Enrollment is for Diabetes Self-Management Education Services. 
Diabetes self-management education is the process of developing the 
customer's knowledge, skills, and abilities that are necessary to manage 
diabetes and improve his or her health outcomes. Vocational Rehabilitation 
(VR) customers might require education about diabetes to address the cause 
of the disease. Diabetes self-management education provides adaptive 
techniques and/or equipment to help the customer self-manage his or her 
diabetes. 
Assessment and teaching of blood sugar monitoring, medication delivery, and 
other self-care skills related to diabetes self-management require close, 
hands-on evaluation and training when working with individuals who are blind 
or visually impaired. 
Diabetes self-management education services are based on the Association of 
Diabetes Care and Education Specialist’s 7 Self-Care Behaviors™, which are: 
• healthy eating; 
• being active;

[page 12]
Open Enrollment No. 3202600156 OE for Diabetes Self-Management v. 1.1 
Page 12 of 60 
• monitoring; 
• taking medications; 
• healthy coping; 
• problem solving; and 
• reducing risk. 
Diabetes self-management education services are for customers who: 
• are newly diagnosed; 
• need surgery or a medical procedure and are at risk of further 
complications because of poor diabetes management; 
• are unable to maintain employment because of their diabetes; 
• need additional training about diabetes management after losing their 
sight; 
• must self-manage diabetes for admittance to training programs and for 
full participation in training such as that offered by the Criss Cole 
Rehabilitation Center; 
• cannot benefit from community-based educational programs; and/or 
• have unique needs that cannot be met through medical providers paid 
through the Maximum Affordable Payment Schedule.

2.5 ASSESSMENT OF DIABETES SELF-MANAGEMENT 
The following sections detail Assessment of Diabetes Self-Management, 
including the information gathered, the recommended equipment, and the 
resulting education and support plan. 
2.5.1 Assessment of Diabetes Self-Management Service Description 
A diabetes self-management assessment is the diabetes educator's evaluation 
of a customer's ability to manage the diabetes. The assessment must gather 
information about the customers: 
• medical history; 
• age; 
• cultural influences; 
• beliefs and attitudes about maintaining good health; and 
• knowledge about diabetes. 
A diabetes self-management assessment is provided in person with the trainer 
and customer at the same location. The diabetes self-management assessment 
may be provided remotely only with a VR director approved VR3472, 
Contracted Service Modification Request, which is provided as Attachment 8 
to this solicitation. Remote services must follow VR-SFP 3.4.8 Remote Service 
Delivery. 
It is recommended that the diabetes educator use adaptive equipment and 
disposable supplies for demonstration during the assessment. The suggested 
items include: 
• a talking blood-glucose meter;

[page 19]
Open Enrollment No. 3202600156 OE for Diabetes Self-Management v. 1.1 
Page 19 of 60 
• an insulin-measuring device, such as Count-A-Dose, which allows a blind 
or vision-impaired individual with diabetes to fill an insulin syringe 
without assistance; 
• a syringe magnifier; 
• a portion-control plate, such as Meal Measure; 
• an insulin pen (or other injectable device for demonstration purposes); 
• a talking blood-pressure monitor; and 
• disposable supplies such as test strips, syringes, and insulin. 
The customer and instructor develop an education and support plan that is 
created from evidence-based approaches for effective health communication 
and education while taking into consideration the customer's barriers to self-
management, abilities, and expectations as well as information from the 
diabetes self-management assessment. (ADA, 2016) 
The initial diabetes self-management assessment helps the diabetes educator 
recommend the skills training from which the customer would benefit. The 
training areas include information and skills relating to: 
• an overview of the pathophysiology of diabetes; 
• nutrition; 
• exercise and activity; 
• blood-glucose monitoring and how to use the monitoring results; 
• diabetes-related complications; 
• management of sick days; 
• medical treatment; 
• medication; 
• foot, skin, and dental care;

• adaptive diabetes self-management equipment and tools.

The diabetes educator develops a written education and support plan in the

VR staff and the diabetes educator ensure that the education and support plan

• cultural influences; 
• learning abilities; and 
• disability. 
Diabetes educators must use the talking blood-glucose meter recommended by

• provide skills training to the customer. 
If the diabetes educator recommends using a different type of talking meter, 
the VR diabetes program specialist must authorize the purchase before the 
equipment is purchased, and skills training occurs.

person centered, informed decision making, the diabetes educator guides the 
customer in the skill of goal setting by assisting them to 
• select an activity that best suits the customer’s self-management needs, 
• help the customer identify strategies and resources for success as well

• plan a course to achieve the goal.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

Are Blind (ILS-OIB) worker submits a referral and issues service authorizations

consequently reduce the benefit of the skills training. If a segment is less than 
two hours, the provider must document on the VR2884, in the Observations 
and Comments section, how this meets the customer’s individual needs. 
The diabetes educator helps the customer develop specific, measurable, 
achievable, realistic, and timely (SMART) goals. 
A new behavior-change goal should be set at each visit between the educator 
and the customer and achievements evaluated at the next visit. The diabetes 
educator helps the customer overcome barriers to success and employ

2.7.1 Post-Training Assessment Service Description 
The diabetes educator conducts post-training assessments no sooner than 30 
calendar days after the skills training is complete. 
As part of the post-training assessment, the diabetes educator: 
• reviews the skills training provided; and 
• reinforces the behavioral changes. 
The post-training assessment must be completed for all customers 30 days

in person, by phone, or by video conferencing with the customer as described 
in VR-SFP 3.4.8 Remote Service Delivery. The preferred method to complete 
the post-training assessment is in person. If a post-training assessment must 
be provided sooner than 30 calendar days after the skills training, the trainer 
must request approval from the referring VR counselor or the OIB worker 
before the post assessment being completed. The VR counselor or OIB worker 
requests approval from the VR director using VR3472, Contracted Service 
Modification Request for Blind and Visually Impaired Services.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

ARTICLE II SCOPE OF WORK 
2.1 OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND 
TWC’s mission is to promote and support a workforce system that creates 
value and offers employers, families, individuals and communities the 
opportunity to achieve and sustain economic prosperity. 
Independent Living Services for Older Individuals who are Blind (ILS-OIB) 
focuses on adjustment to blindness and development of skills so that 
customers can live confidently and independently in their homes and 
communities. The program's goals are to empower individuals with disabilities; 
maximize their leadership potential, independence, and productivity; and 
ensure their integration and full inclusion in society. 
The ILS-OIB program promotes independent living by encouraging self-control, 
self-help, and self-determination, and by promoting equal access and 
individual and systemic advocacy. The program assists customers address the 
impact of their loss of vision so that each customer can achieve their 
independent living goals. 
ILS-OIB helps customers: 
• who are age 55 and older;

2.3.2 Independent Living Skills Training 
Independent Living Skills (ILS) Training aims to empower customers to live 
more independently. The following section details the range of services 
offered, the roles of the OIB worker and IL skills provider, and the 
requirements for payment. 
2.3.2.1 SERVICE DESCRIPTION 
Providers of IL skills services offer a variety of services in the customer's home 
or community. 
Providers may provide one or more of the following, as authorized by the OIB 
worker: 
• Application Assessment—the process of gathering referral data and 
information about the customer's preliminary need for services. The 
information, along with eye medical reports, is used by the OIB worker 
to determine an individual's eligibility for the ILS-OIB program. 
• Comprehensive Assessment—the process of working with the customer 
to identify the issues that prevent him or her from functioning 
independently. The assessment, which occurs after the OIB worker 
determines eligibility, can also help a customer maintain or increase his 
or her independence. Comprehensive assessment includes listening to 
the customer describe problems related to the loss of vision, conducting

[page 15]
Open Enrollment No. 3202600157 OE for Independent Living Services for Older Individuals 
who are Blind 
v. 1.1 Page 15 of 44 
an in-depth interview to gather information, observing as the customer 
demonstrates his or her skills at home, and talking with family members 
or caregivers to gather any additional information. The comprehensive 
assessment is used by the OIB worker to develop the Independent Living 
Plan (ILP). 
• Independent Living Skills Training—training in techniques that enable a 
customer to perform daily living skills in alternative ways. IL skills are 
divided into the following categories: 
o Personal management—including grooming, eating, health, safety, 
clothing identification and coordination, and the use of medications 
o Home management—including sewing, cleaning of clothing, 
housekeeping, meal preparation and kitchen safety skills, planning 
for grocery shopping, and minor home maintenance 
o Communication—including telling time and time management, 
using the telephone, money management, writing, organization, 
and using adaptive devices 
o Information access and technology—including training on the use 
of magnifiers, CCTVs, and other devices for low-vision, as well as 
adaptations of computers and other types of technology. 
• Information and Referral (I&R) services that help the customer identify 
and use alternative resources, such as Meals on Wheels and the Texas 
State Library to meet his or her individual needs. I&R services can be 
provided at any point in the independent living process.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

ARTICLE I PURPOSE 
The Texas Workforce Commission (TWC) is accepting proposals to establish 
contracts with qualified entities, including for-profit companies, nonprofit 
organizations, and private colleges and universities, to deliver instructor-led, 
short-duration training to Vocational Rehabilitation (VR) customers. These 
training services are designed to enhance vocational skills, support 
employment outcomes, and promote customer independence. Training 
durations typically range from one (1) to four (4) weeks but may extend up 
to six (6) months depending on the customer’s individualized employment 
plan. Procurement Services (PS) will administer the procurement process for 
this Solicitation, which includes Solicitation publication, handling of 
communications from vendors, as well as managing the receipt of Proposals 
for review and evaluation.  
Information regarding TWC and its programs is available online and can 
currently be accessed at www.twc.texas.gov.

referring them to training services designed to help individuals explore, 
develop, and attain skills that support competitive integrated employment or 
independent living. Referrals are based on each customer’s employment or 
education goals as outlined in their Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) 
or Independent Living Plan (ILP).

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

7 Scope of Work (SOW) 
7.1 Scope of Services to be Performed 
The required services to be provided are armed security guard services at 1716 Parkway Dr 
Lubbock, TX 79403. 
Armed Security Guard:  
a) Security Guards must be licensed to carry a firearm according to state regulations and 
have at least one (1) year of documented experience in the security industry. 
Documentation of experience must be supplied to HHSC for each Security Guard 
assigned to a post. Any new personnel must also supply satisfactory documentation of 
experience prior to their initial assignment to a post.  
b) The Security Guard should be fluent in English and able to communicate clearly both 
verbally and in writing.  
c) No Security Guard shall be paid for overtime duty or for days that the offices are closed 
for official State holidays. It will be the responsibility of the awarded contractor to 
ensure each officer is relieved and rotated appropriately to negate overtime.  
d) Security Guards will report on time, in uniform at all times while on duty, oriented to 
security duties, properly instructed, supervised and with completed background checks.  
A copy of the background check must be provided to HHSC prior to the security guard 
starting.  
e) The Security Guard shall report to the appointed HHSC authorized representative for 
each site assigned. Names and phone numbers of each security guard will be provided 
by the Contractor’s contract manager.  
f) The Security Guard will limit telephone calls to emergency and official business use only. 
If using a state agency phone, collect and long -distance calls are not permitted. Misuse 
of state agency phones could lead to termination of the contract. Use of sta te agency 
computers, copiers or any other state -owned equipment is not permitted. Guards will 
not occupy a private office with agency facilities or engage in lengthy personal

[page 12]
PCS 137 - SERVICES 
Version 2.10 Page 12 of 42 Revised 03/18/2026 
conversations or other activities other than providing continuous security services as 
specified herein. Security Guards are only permitted to use personal cell phones on 
breaks or while at lunch. 
g) Security guard shall be given a thirty-minute (30) minute lunch to be taken at different 
times each day between the hours of 11:30am to 1:30pm. The Security Guard shall 
notify HHSC prior to leaving post for lunch.  
h) Security guard, after informing appropriate staff, may take a fifteen (15) minute break 
during the first half of their shift and a fifteen (15) minute break during the last half of 
their shift. Guard will take breaks while on the premises, after notifying the authorized 
HHSC representative at location.  
i) The Security Guard shall make rounds of the premises randomly and as requested by 
the HHSC authorized representative. When not conducting rounds of the premises, the 
Security Guard will remain at the designated security station located within or near the 
office lobby area. The Security Guard will notify the HHSC authorized representative 
should it become necessary to leave the security station for reasons other than 
conducting rounds or responding to a security emergency.  The Security Guard shall 
notify HHSC prior to leaving post. 
j) The Security Guard shall at no time leave the designated premises while on assigned 
duty without an approved replacement being present.  
k) The Security Guard shall address any person who is continuously loud or boisterous in 
an office to refrain from such action or escort those individuals from the premises. In 
the event of a conflict between an HHSC employee and a client, the Security Guard shall 
make his/her presence known and render assistance to include contacting the 
authorities. The Security Guard shall notify HHSC when the authorities are called and 
document the incident in detail in the incident report.  
l) The Security Guard will check identification of all persons entering the building during 
and after "normal” office hours when deemed appropriate by the HHSC authorized 
representative. Any person without an employee identification badge must sign in and 
out and will be issued a visitor’s badge before entering a restricted area. The Security 
Guard will permit only authorized persons to enter restricted areas of the premises.  
m) The Security Guard will not engage in conversations with clients and/or employees and 
will not give any policy/office procedures information to clients. Security guard will refer 
questions from clients to the receptionist.  
n) No Security Guard shall perform office work or any other work pertaining to HHSC other 
than those services for which the Security Guard has been contracted to perform.  
o) The Security Guard will check all interior areas of leased space before going off duty to 
ascertain if any staff and/or clients remain in the building. The guard will then check all 
exterior doors to be sure the building is locked and secure. If a guard’s shift is completed 
prior to the office closing, the guard will check all areas before leaving the premises and 
report any areas of concern to the HHSC authorized representative.

[page 13]
PCS 137 - SERVICES 
Version 2.10 Page 13 of 42 Revised 03/18/2026 
p) The Security Guard must be thoroughly familiar with the operation and control of all 
building life safety systems such as but not limited to fire alarms, building life safety 
system, telephone system, and access and intrusion alarm systems. Security Guard shall 
follow the policy set forth by the HHSC authorized representative. Required documents 
will be provided to the awarded vendor on first day of work.  
q) The Security Guard shall be available to escort HHSC employees to their cars if a security 
risk exists.  
r) The Security Guard will prevent employees and visitors of HHSC from harassment, 
incursion, or any criminal activity by unauthorized persons while on HHSC premises.  
s) All security guards shall be thoroughly familiar with Health and Human Services 
Commission building security. Special attention shall be given to the procedures for 
afterhours building access and emergency procedures for fires and bomb threats, 
including the Office Emergency Action Plan (OEAP). The OEAP plan is available at each 
HHSC office. Guards will become familiar with all emergency phone numbers and facility 
evacuation plans.  
t) The Security Guard will report any unusual incidents, hazardous conditions, or 
emergencies to the appropriate authority i.e. City Police Dept., City Fire Dept., and HHSC 
authorized representative.  
u) The Security Guard will not be asked to perform duties other than that of providing 
guard service as outlined in the SOW.  
v) Awarded Contractor shall furnish all labor, tools, transportation, equipment, materials, 
and supplies, as necessary. Awarded contractor shall be responsible for supervision, 
clean up and disposal, and must have all applicable permits, licenses, and insurance 
coverage.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

coordinate the planning and delivery of health and human services in Texas. It is established 
pursuant to Chapter 523, Texas Government Code and is responsible for oversight of Texas 
Health and Human Services agencies.

7 Scope of Work (SOW) 
7.1 Scope of Services to be Performed 
The required services to be provided are to support the work of Family Resource Centers 
(FRCs). Training and technical assistance activities are outlined below.  
a) Provide on-going training and technical assistance as needed for Family Support Services 
(FSS) selected grantees implementing an FRC. Training will cover areas such as: 
a. Work with individuals and families that are represented in a community and 
programs and services. 
b. Work with individuals and families that are represented in a community, in 
programs, and in services. 
c. Strong collaborative relationships between staff and families. 
d. Strengths-based approach to service delivery. 
e. Focus on  improving the well-being of children and families. 
f. Involvement of peers, neighbors, and communities. 
g. Coordination of multiple services; and 
h. High-quality staff training and coaching. 
 
b) Provide training and on-going technical assistance to the FSS selected grantees on the 
following topics:  
a. On-boarding including training on FRC implementation. 
b. How to incorporate family voice and parent leadership into implementation 
design. 
c. FRC evaluation strategies and best practices. 
d. Strategies to improve design. 
e. Outreach, family engagement, and community collaboration strategies for FRCs. 
f. The role that staff can play at the FRC.

[page 12]
PCS 137 - SERVICES 
Version 2.10 Page 12 of 40 Revised 03/18/2026 
g. The core services of an FRC which include parent leadership development, 
resource and referral, parenting support, child development activities, and 
community strengthening.  
c) Provide on-going learning opportunities with FRC grantees through monthly or 
bimonthly webinars as needed. 
d) Provide individualized technical assistance to FSS selected grantees specific to their 
plans for implementation. 
e) Create an FSS FRC technical assistance plan including: 
a. Technical assistance plan for each of the established sites including: 
i. Monthly Peer Collaborative virtual meetings 
ii. All communication designated for all FRC grantees must be reviewed and 
approved by the FSS point of contact prior to being sent out the FRC 
cohort.  This includes Monthly Peer Collaborative calendar invitations and 
Month Peer Collaborative recap emails.   
iii. A minimum of quarterly individual site technical assistance or requested 
by FSS selected grantee.  Technical assistance for FSS selected grantees 
will be up to 60 hours and will be determined in collaboration with HHSC. 
iv. Coordinate peer sharing between established sites and new FRC sites. 
v. Conduct an in-person site visit for six FSS selected grantees at least once 
every three years. This will ensure all FRC sites have in-person site visits 
on a rotating schedule that meets the needs of FSS and selected grantees.  
Combining visits to other sites in close proximity is encouraged to 
maximize travel. 
vi. All communication regarding an in-person site visit with an FSS selected 
grantee should include the FSS point of contact and the selected grantee.  
The in-person site visit should be planned for a time when the FSS 
selected grantee and FSS point of contact is available.  
b. Individualized technical assistance plan for new FRC sites including: 
i. Coordinate peer sharing between established sites and new sites. 
ii. Complete a kickoff meeting for new cohort groups to include established 
cohort groups. 
iii. Invite and welcome new FRC sites to the monthly cohort peer 
collaborative meetings. 
iv. Provide individual site technical assistance monthly within the first six 
months of the implementing year then every two months for the

[page 13]
PCS 137 - SERVICES 
Version 2.10 Page 13 of 40 Revised 03/18/2026 
remaining six months. Provide additional assistance as requested by FSS 
or the site. 
v. Conduct an in-person site visit within the first year implementing a new 
site then at least once every three years. Combining visits to other sites in 
close proximity is encourages to maximize travel. 
c.  Encourage FSS FRC grantees to connect outside of regularly scheduled meetings 
and to visit one another’s sites. 
d. Offer trainings for FRCs as need is determined. All training content must be 
reviewed and approved by HHSC/FSS.   
f) Schedule and lead a virtual or in-person meetings at least every two months with FSS to 
determine the best implementation, integration, and collaboration efforts.  
g) Provide by email, monthly reports to the FSS Point of Contact that include: 
a. Status updates for each FSS selected grantee. 
b. Program successes and challenges. 
c. Trends from individualized technical assistance provided to selected grantees. 
d. The amount of technical assistance hours administered that month. 
e. A summary of the site visits conducted that month 
f. Recommended future planning. 
h) Provide, by email, awareness of communication with other entities, national partners, 
other states, and so on as it relates to FRCs when appropriate to maintain coordination 
in effort to the FSS Point of Contact.  
i) Coordinate and co-host with FSS an annual in-person statewide FRC gathering to 
promote networking, training, and peer driven learning opportunities. 
a. The contractor will be responsible for setting the agenda, providing speakers, 
and planning and executing the FRC Grantee Meeting. 
b. All agenda, speakers and presentation materials must be approved by HHSC. 
c. The contractor will provide a proposed timeline for FRC Grantee Meeting two 
months before the event for review and approval by FSS/HHSC.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

a) Service locations are in HHSC Region 6 as follows:

 The Map (PDF) of HHSC Regions may be accessed at:
