b) Changes to service location(s) include but are not limited to: new office space within

footage, expansion of an office into multiple offices, and relocation of office.  
7.1.2 Performance Schedule 
Contractor shall perform the contracted services, including any minor adjustment call -back 
services, Monday through Friday between the hours 7 a.m. to 7 p.m (Central Time). Contractor 
shall not interfere with normal flow of HHSC business at any service location. 
Contractor shall respond to all service calls within four (4) hours of HHSC request, unless the 
Response Deadline is extended by the HHS C Contract Manager. 
7.1.3 Services Outside Regular Business Hours 
Any services performed outside of standard office hours 7 a.m. to 7 p.m Central Time) must be 
requested and approved in writing by the HHSC Contract Manager and will be paid at the rate 
stated in Exhibit C – Pricing Sheet.  
Services performed outside of standard office hours without HHSC prior written approval shalll 
be at Contractor’s own risk and will be billed at the established service rate  stated in Exhibit C – 
Pricing Sheet. 
HHSC reserves the right to declare any requested services an emergency during standard office  
hours or outside standard office hours and will request emergency services in writing. 
Contractor shall respond to requests for emergency deployment of Commissioned Peace 
Officers to specific locations within one (1) hour of notification from HHSC and continue work 
until the services requested are complete to the satisfaction of HHSC. 
7.1.4 State Holidays 
State holidays observed are maintained by the State Auditor’s Office and may be accessed at: 
https://hr.sao.texas.gov/Holidays . HHSC does not require services to be performed on the  “All

9.2.1 Price Adjustment Index 
Price adjustments are not automatic. Prices only may be adjusted at the sole discretion of 
HHSC. 
HHSC may permit price adjustments when correlated with the index as specified below 
and as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), Region VI, Washington, DC 
20212. 
BLS Website: https://data.bls.gov/cgi -bin/srgate 
CPI-W Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers – Series ID: CWURR0000AA0 : 
https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/CWUR0000AA0  
CPI-U All Urban Consumers – Series ID: CUUR0000AA0  
https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/CUUR0000AA0  
When using the most recent monthly information from the index, the following applies:  
A = Index from the month of the Response Deadline of this IFB, OR 
The effective date/month of the last approved price increase or renewal option 
exercised, whichever is later.  
B = Current or latest baseline index  
The allowable percent change must be calculated as follows:  
B-A ÷ A x 100% = Percent of allowable price increase or decrease  
Failure by the Contractor to calculate this formula and provide any supporting documentation 
will not be considered a properly submitted price increase request  and will result in rejection of 
the price increase request. 
The Contractor may offer price decreases in excess of the allowable percent change at any time 
during the term of the Contract.  
9.2.2 Price Adjustment Requests 
Contractor must provide, in writing to the HHS C Contract Manager, a request for a price 
adjustment. The adjustment request must use the index and formula identified in Section 9.2.1 
(Price Adjustment Index). Only contracts with renewals are eligible for CPI increases  and must 
be completed prior to the start of the renewal period.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

7 Scope of Work (SOW) 
7.1 Scope of Services to be Performed 
The Contractor shall train and provide ongoing support to HHSC and DSHS staff with a focus on 
the compliance and applicability of the Uniform Guidance 2 CFR Part 200. The Contractor shall 
be responsible for monitoring and incorporating any revisions to 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform 
Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards . 
The Contractor shall provide instructor -led training presentation(s)  delivered via Onsite Training 
as well as Webcast Training. The Contractor shall be solely responsible for the hosting, 
maintenance, and operation of a dedicated website (the 'Registration Site') for the express 
purpose of capturing, managing, and tracking all training registrations. HHS may request 
registration and proof of completion. Having the training offered in different formats allows the 
participants to choose the best learning styl e for themselves and offers multiple dates to 
accommodate their schedules. Each participant will receive twelve (12) contact hours of federal 
grant management training upon completion.  
Contractor shall provide online access to training and course materials after completion of the 
training(s) to HHSC and DSHS staff for additional support. Electronic versions of supporting 
course materials, in a searchable pdf format, must be provided for each attendee. The 
participants must have access to an electronic version of a reference handbook available for 
download or email. The Contractor shall be available to provide technical assistance. 
Training Content and Materials.  Contractor shall provide the training agenda and materials to 
HHSC’s point of contact fourteen (14) Business Days before the scheduled onsite and the 
scheduled web-based to distribute the training information to participants.   Any requested 
edits must be re-reviewed by HHSC’s point of contact.  HHSC will approve the training materials 
within five (5) Business Days of receipt.  
Changes to Training Content and Materials. Contractor must update all relevant  training 
presentation materials and agendas and resubmit them to HHSC’s designated point of contact

[page 12]
PCS 137 - SERVICES 
Version 2.10 Page 12 of 41 Revised 03/18/2026 
for review and approval no later than  five (5) Business Days after identification of the change 
prior to the trainings. 
The grant management training will consist of two (2) in -person trainings led by one to two 
instructors and two (2) webcast training sessions per year  of the Contract.  
 
a) Onsite training for up to 200 participants:  
Training will be held at 4601 W. Guadalupe Austin, Texas, 78751 , or alternate nearby 
location, for two (2) days from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. with one (1) hour for lunch each 
day. HHSC will coordinate with Contractor if alternate location will be required and will 
provide advance notice. 
 
b) Live Webcast Training (Virtual) for up to 100 participants per session: 
The Live Webcast Training will be exactly like the onsite training, except it will be held 
virtually.  Attendees will have twenty-four seven (24/7) access to register on the 
Contractor website for training and videos, and participants will gain access to the 
online resource center, guides, templates, checklists, and more, all designed to help 
manage federal grants. All participants will have one (1) year to complete the virtual 
training from participant’s registration date or by Contract termination date, whichever 
is the sooner date.  
 
c) Training materials will include :  
 
1. Changes in the Administrative Requirements and Cost Principles contained in 2 CFR 
Part 200: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title -2/subtitle-A/chapter-II/part-200 
2. Getting started with federal award - Managing risk, pre-award requirements, and 
types of agreements: eCFR :: 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart C -- Pre-Federal Award 
Requirements and Contents of Federal Awards 
3. Monitoring and reporting requirements for federal funding - Budget revisions, 
financial management, and payment management: eCFR :: 32 CFR Part 34 -- 
Administrative Requirements for Grants and Agreements with For -Profit 
Organizations 
4. Procurement standards - Best practices and requirements, procurement methods, 
procedures, conflicts of interest, and competition: eCFR :: 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart D - 
Procurement Standards 
5. Property management standards - Property types, title, and disposal: eCFR :: 2 CFR 
Part 200 Subpart D - Property Standards  
d) Types of Trainings Videos shall include: 
1. Closing out awards - Wrapping up awards and record retention . Video will be 
provided by contractor on this topic.  
2. Direct costs and indirect costs - Basics of cost allocation . Video will be provided by 
contractor on this topic.

[page 13]

3. Grant Management - It Takes Village. Internal control, time and effort, and public 
policy requirements -video will be provided by contractor on this topic.  
4. Surviving the Single Audit. Cost basics . Common types of allowable and unallowable 
costs and the general rules for cost allowability - video will be provided by 
contractor on this topic. 
5. E-mentoring. Participants who complete either the onsite or virtual training program 
will be provided with access to comprehensive resources, including a digital library, 
training recordings, and direct support via email or telephone to facilitate the 
application of training principles within their professional roles . Access period falls 
within the Contract term, including any exercised renewals.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

9.2.1 Price Adjustment Index 
Price adjustments are not automatic. Prices only may be adjusted at the sole discretion of

HHSC may permit price adjustments when correlated with the index as specified below 
and as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), Region VI, Washington, DC

BLS Website: https://data.bls.gov/cgi -bin/srgate 
CPI-W Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers – Series ID: CWURR0000AA0 :

CPI-U All Urban Consumers – Series ID: CUUR0000AA0  
https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/CUUR0000AA0  
When using the most recent monthly information from the index, the following applies:  
A = Index from the month of the Response Deadline of this IFB, OR 
The effective date/month of the last approved price increase or renewal option 
exercised, whichever is later.  
B = Current or latest baseline index  
The allowable percent change must be calculated as follows:  
B-A ÷ A x 100% = Percent of allowable price increase or decrease  
Failure by the Contractor to calculate this formula and provide any supporting documentation 
will not be considered a properly submitted price increase request  and will result in rejection of 
the price increase request. 
The Contractor may offer price decreases in excess of the allowable percent change at any time 
during the term of the Contract.

must be completed prior to the start of the renewal period. 
Contractor must provide supporting documentation to justify any price adjustment. Any 
request submitted that fails to use the formula above for calculating a price adjustment will not

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

9 Pricing Information 
9.1 Pricing Structure 
Prices offered, as part of the Bidder’s response, must be firm, fixed prices for the life of the 
Contract. 
The pricing must be submitted only using Exhibit C - Pricing Sheet based on the description and 
the unit of measure(s) provided for each line item. The unit prices must include all IFB 
requirements, including, but not limited to, labor, equipment, materials, supplies and all related 
expenses. 
9.2 Price Adjustments 
Contractors are required to immediately implement any price decrease that become available 
during the Contract term. Contractor must notify the designated HHSC Contract Manager in 
writing so that a Purchase Order Change Notice or Contract Amendment may be processed. The 
Contractor will be provided the HHS Agency Contract Manager contact information upon 
award. 
9.2.1 Price Adjustment Index 
Price adjustments are not automatic. Prices only may be adjusted at the sole discretion of 
HHSC. 
HHSC may permit price adjustments when correlated with the index as specified below 
and as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), Region VI, Washington, DC 
20212.

CPI-U All Urban Consumers – Series ID: CUUR0000AA0

When using the most recent monthly information from the index, the following applies:  
A = Index from the month of the Response Deadline of this IFB, OR 
The effective date/month of the last approved price increase or renewal option 
exercised, whichever is later. 
B = Current or latest baseline index 
The allowable percent change must be calculated as follows:  
B-A ÷ A x 100% = Percent of allowable price increase or decrease 
Failure by the Contractor to calculate this formula and provide any supporting documentation 
will not be considered a properly submitted price increase request and will result in rejection of 
the price increase request. 
The Contractor may offer price decreases in excess of the allowable percent change at any time 
during the term of the Contract. 
9.2.2 Price Adjustment Requests 
The Contractor must provide, in writing to the HHS Agency Contract Manager, a request for a 
price adjustment. The adjustment request must use the index and formula identified in Section 
9.2.1 (Price Adjustment Index). Only contracts with renewals are eligible for CPI increases and 
must be completed prior to the start of the renewal period. 
Contractor must provide supporting documentation to justify any price adjustment. Any 
request submitted that fails to use the formula above for calculating a price adjustment will not 
be considered a complete, properly submitted request and will be rejected. Additionally, any 
request submitted that does not include supporting documentation will not be considered a 
complete, properly submitted price adjustment request and will be rejected. 
The HHS Agency reserves the right to accept or reject the request for a price adjustment. The 
Contractor will receive written notification, through a Purchase Order Change Notice or 
Contract Amendment, from the HHS Agency Contract Manager documenting action taken, to 
include effective dates, for any adjustments approved. 
9.2.3 Discounts 
If Contractor at any time during the term of the Contract provides a discount on the final 
contract costs, Contractor will notify HHSC in writing at least ten (10) calendar days prior to the

Rate, published by the U.S. Department of Labor (USDOL), if applicable.

prior to the date the written request is received by HHSC. Notification of an approved increase 
in the Contract rate will be provided through a Purchase Order Change Notice or Contract 
Amendment from the HHS Agency Contract Manager to include the new unit price and

The HHS Agency Contract Manager is required to report vendor performance for purchases 
over $25,000 through the Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts (CPA) Vendor Performance 
Tracking System (VPTS). The VPTS reporting is required throughout the life of a contract and not

Performance Notification – Non-Material Deficiency 
The HHS Agency may notify Contractor in writing of specific areas of the Contractor’s 
performance that fail to meet performance expectations, standards, or schedules, but that, in 
the determination of the HHS Agency, do not result in a material deficiency or delay in the 
implementation or operation of the services. 
12.4 Contractor Response to Notification of Non-Material Deficiency 
The Contractor shall, within three (3) business days (or another date approved by the HHS 
Agency) of receipt of written notice of a non-material deficiency, provide the HHS Agency 
Contract Manager a written response that: 
a) Explains the reasons for the deficiency, the Contractor’s plan to address or cure the 
deficiency, and when the deficiency will be cured. 
The Contractor’s noncompliance or failure to timely correct  the deficiency may result in 
delayed payment or non-payment as determined by the HHS Agency. 
12.5 Corrective Action Plan (The Plan) 
At its discretion, the HHS Agency may require the Contractor to submit a detailed written 
Corrective Action Plan and include how the Contractor will correct or resolve a performance 
issue, deficiency, or a breach of this Contract. 
The Plan, at a minimum, must include, but is not limited to:  
a) A detailed explanation of the reasons for the cited deficiency; 
b) The Contractor’s assessment or diagnosis of the cause; and 
c) A specific proposal to cure or resolve the deficiency to include a timeline for 
implementation. 
The Plan must be submitted by the deadline set forth in the HHS Agency’s request. 
The Plan is subject to HHS Agency approval.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.

You extract compliance matrices from US state/local government RFPs.

A compliance matrix is the complete list of things a vendor must do, provide, or satisfy to submit a responsive proposal. Missing a single "shall" can disqualify a bid, so recall matters more than brevity.

Extract every requirement that meets ANY of these tests:
- Binding language: shall, must, will (vendor obligation), is required to, may not.
- Advisory language directed at the vendor: should, is encouraged to.
- Administrative facts a bidder must act on: submission deadlines, question deadlines, conference dates, required forms, page limits, copy counts, delivery addresses, eligibility/certification prerequisites, evaluation criteria and weights.

Rules:
1. verbatim_text is the EXACT sentence(s) from the RFP. Never paraphrase, never summarize, never fix typos. Trim only surrounding boilerplate.
2. One requirement per row. If a sentence contains two independent obligations, split it into two rows repeating the shared text.
3. section_ref is the RFP's own numbering (e.g. "3.2.1", "Section IV.B"). Use the nearest numbered heading if the sentence itself is unnumbered.
4. type: "shall" for binding (shall/must/will/required), "should" for advisory, "info" for administrative facts with no modal verb.
5. category: eligibility | deliverable | deadline | form | evaluation. Pick the single best fit; deadlines with dates always get category "deadline" and an ISO due_date.
6. page is the PDF page number where the text appears (1-indexed).
7. id values are sequential: R-001, R-002, ... in document order.
8. Do NOT invent requirements. If the document is not an RFP or has no requirements, return an empty requirements array.
